messages.author: 066a0ceb2819d0e3
messages.subject: File permission problem too
parts:
I installed rApache a few months ago and it was working fine then, but
now when I tried to run it it didn't work, so I decided to upgrade
it. I am using R 2.11.1, ubuntu 10.04, and rApache 1.1.9. I use the
quick install for ubuntu method. Configure works fine, but when I run
'sudo make' I get an error on the /home/bosr/rapache-1.1.9/test/
httpd.conf file. I tried to chmod 777 the file, but that didn't
help. Seems like trivial problem but it won't let me continue. I am
happy to modify the httpd.conf file myself once I get rApache
installed and working. Can anyone point me in the right direction?

Thanks,

Roger

messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Re: File permission problem too
parts:
You shouldn't have to use sudo just to make rapache. As you may have a mixture of files created by your username and those by root, try starting over with  the tar/config/make  commands executed as your username only.

Jeff

messages.author: 596788cb1219e353
messages.subject: Re: File permission problem too
parts:
Hi Roger,

configure takes arguments.

My OS and R versions are identical.  Install the Ubuntu packages libapache2-mod-apreq2
and apache2-prefork-dev.   The latter contains apxs2 binary for apache2-mpm-prefork.

To get the configure command to recognize the system libraries, run it with the --with-R, --with-apache2-apxs, and --with-apreq2-config options.

When configure is done, Jeff Horner suggested using a script to fuss with libapreq2.la.  I filed this as bug 651396 in Launchpad against Ubuntu 10 (lucid).

The script below is close to what I did today.  It runs inside the rapache-1.1.10 directory.

#!/bin/sh
PATH=.:/usr/share/ant/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
unset R_HOME
make clean
configure --with-R=/usr/local/bin/R --with-apache2-apxs=/usr/bin/apxs2 \
--with-apreq2-config=/usr/bin/apreq2-config
if test -f /usr/bin/lsb_release -a `/usr/bin/lsb_release -cs` = "lucid"; then \
   cp /usr/lib/libapreq2.la libapreq2.la~; \
        sed -e "s/\/usr\/lib\/libuuid.la/-luuid/g;s/libdir='\/lib/libdir='\/usr\/lib/g" \
            < libapreq2.la~ > libapreq2.la; \
fi;
make
sudo make install
